decisions.question: H6 added NidanaModule (flutter-binding@v2 G20, Refinement 8). Which Flutter module binding does the integration module-scope slice prove end to end: the route observer the example already uses, the new wrapper widget, or both?

options.label: Both bindings, same scenario
options.consequence: The checkout module's lifetime (in-subtree navigation through the grace period, exit teardown, re-entry with retained state) is proven under ModuleScopeObserver and again under NidanaModule in the composed app. Costs a binding switch in the example's shell and a second run of the module tests; H21 must place it within a phase's size window.

options.label: NidanaModule only
options.consequence: The example drops ModuleScopeObserver. G10 and Refinement 3 then have no end-to-end proof, while the .6 deep-link slice and flutter-binding@v2 G16 ('with the module scopes their paths match acquired') are written around the observer.

options.label: ModuleScopeObserver only
options.consequence: No change to the example. NidanaModule, which Spec §7.3 now names as the binding that works with any router, is proven only by nidana.flutter.8's own gate against stand-in pages, never against the composed app with real MaterialPageRoute transitions.

decisions.why: Spec §7.3's Flutter row now offers two alternative bindings, and flutter-binding@v2 guarantees both (G10, G20). This node exists to prove the composed packages, and the two bindings differ in what an adopter sees: the wrapper releases when a popped page's exit transition ends, later than the observer (Refinement 8, N1), so the grace-period behavior in the composed app is not implied by the observer's slice. The example runs on Flutter's own Navigator with named routes, so the observer stays valid, and the wrapper reads no route name, so it runs on the same Navigator with no new dependency (ADR-002 item 3's row stays as it is). Close call against 'ModuleScopeObserver only'. The signal that would have favored it: H21 finding that the second binding cannot fit any phase's size window without a new phase.
evidence: hsdd/contract/flutter-binding.md Refinement 1, Refinement 8, G10, G16, G20, Delivery
docs/auto-run/experiments/flutter-binding-v0151/ (N1 to N6, cited by flutter-binding@v2 Refinement 8)

decisions.question: Spec §7.2 'Scope timing' has two halves: a MODULE or PAGE activation before start() is rejected, and an APPLICATION activation after start() is allowed with a dev-mode diagnostic. Which halves does the new scope-timing slice own?

options.label: Rejection half only, with the example's start-before-UI order
options.consequence: The slice proves that the example's bootstrap (start() once APPLICATION topologies, services and executor are in place, before the UI mounts) binds every page and module scope on a running bus, and that the same bindings before start() are rejected and bind nothing. The late APPLICATION diagnostic is proven only by bus-api@v2's own cases, which the unrestricted replay runs.

options.label: Both halves
options.consequence: The example gains a late-loaded APPLICATION feature, a scenario Guide Appendix A does not have, to show a dev-mode diagnostic (bus-api@v2 G22) that no other slice reads.

decisions.chosen: Rejection half only, with the example's start-before-UI order
decisions.why: The H20 prompt names the rejection. The example follows Guide Appendix A, trimmed (plan decision D5), and no primary flow there loads a feature late, so the late-activation diagnostic would be a scenario added only to replay a guarantee that bus-api@v2's fixtures already pin and that nidana.integration.6 to .8 replay unrestricted. The signal that would have changed my mind: a primary flow of the reference scenario that loads an APPLICATION feature after start().

decisions.why: The scope-timing slice reads §7.2 and §7.1's APPLICATION row; the module slice reads §7.3's Flutter row, Appendix A.8 and Guide Appendix B.3 (L7's passages). decisions.question: The prompt names three slices to restate (bootstrap, scope timing, module scope). v0.15.1 also changes what the hydration slice relies on (Spec §7.2: hydration arrives after start() as events, folded by reducers already active) and what bootstrap connects (Spec §3.13 step 1 also connects bootstrap subscriptions). Restate those too, or leave them?

options.label: Restate hydration and the bootstrap subscriptions
options.consequence: Hydration reads 'publishing a loaded value as an event after start(), a reducer topology already active' with §7.2 cited; the bootstrap slice names the service subscriptions made during bootstrap and their connection after the topologies. The Owns list then states the order the example's main already follows (start(), then hydrate(), then runApp, plan .6).

options.label: Restate only the three named slices
options.consequence: Hydration stays true but silent on the order Spec §7.2 now makes the reason scope timing costs nothing; the bootstrap slice omits the payment service's subscription, which start() connects in its own step.

decisions.chosen: Restate hydration and the bootstrap subscriptions
decisions.why: Neither restatement changes a guarantee or a phase; both make the Owns list say what v0.15.1 now says about the same slices, and the hydration order is the premise of Spec §7.2's scope-timing argument, which the new slice proves. No evidence beyond the Spec text was needed.
